reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: The trial achieved 100% engraftment (16/16 patients), confirming that the allogeneic stem cell transplantation successfully engaged the hematopoietic system. The conditioning regimen components (fludarabine, melphalan) also achieved their intended lymphodepletion effects as evidenced by successful engraftment. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: The intended mechanisms were activated - lymphocyte depletion occurred (enabling engraftment), and graft-versus-tumor immunity was established as evidenced by the differential outcomes between donor types. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: The clinical outcomes were mixed and donor-dependent. Related donor recipients showed better long-term survival (effect size 4.0), while all unrelated donor recipients died by 2 years (effect size 1.0). This suggests the mechanism works but is highly dependent on donor compatibility. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: Clear subgroup effect - related donor recipients had substantially better outcomes than unrelated donor recipients, indicating the intervention works in a specific subpopulation. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Small sample size (n=16) limits power, but the clear donor-type effect suggests biological rather than statistical issues. High toxicity rates (25% respiratory failure, 16.7% multi-organ failure) may have limited efficacy in the unrelated donor group.
